first.rationale: Onboarding completion and activation are both deteriorating, and memories 86 and 31 indicate that reducing onboarding and signup friction can improve both outcomes durably. This is more directly aligned with sustainable qualified revenue than reacting immediately with discounts. Memory 73 should also be verified because promotional pricing is the strongest alternative given competitor pressure, but its effects on retention, margin, and long-term customer quality remain uncertain. The onboarding test should therefore measure downstream qualified-revenue signals, not completion alone.

final.rationale: Run a standard experiment shortening onboarding for self-serve SMB accounts. The confirmed onboarding result improved completion, time-to-value, and 30-day retention, directly addressing both current declines. Signup simplification also increased SMB activation and qualified revenue, though its slight retention decline means the experiment must guard on 30-day retention and measure qualified revenue rather than completion alone. Promotional pricing is rejected despite acquisition lift because the verified cohort suffered severe retention loss and failed to survive the first renewal cycle. Uncertainty remains about whether prior onboarding effects fully replicate under current competitive conditions.
